wave: VERIFICATION BLINDNESS -- InventoryReport::is_closed() (core/src/census/mod.rs), the pure function that gates runtime::systemize's real INVENTORY_ACCOUNTING_NOT_CLOSED coding-admission blocker, had zero direct unit test coverage anywhere in the workspace. Its siblings CensusReport::is_closed() and NormalizationReport::is_closed() (core/src/schema/mod.rs) both carry dedicated positive AND negative closure tests; InventoryReport's had neither.
wave_title: Twenty-fourth generation this cycle. After generations 20-23 closed out the unescaped-delimiter-join bug class, pivoted the investigative angle (per the standing priority order) back to verification blindness -- auditing whether existing accounting/closure invariants are actually exercised by tests, the same angle that found real gaps in generations 18-19. Surveyed every `is_closed()` implementation in the workspace (CensusReport, NormalizationReport, DependencyClosureReport, InventoryReport) and found InventoryReport's was the one outlier with no coverage at all.
priority_classification: verification blindness -- not a live production bug (every real production constructor, InventoryReport::new, keeps artifacts_total/dispositions mutually consistent by construction, so is_closed() is always true on any report this codebase actually builds today), but a real gap in this project's own verification coverage: a regression that silently broke is_closed()'s logic (e.g. an accidental `true` literal, or comparing against the wrong field) would go completely undetected -- confirmed directly by grepping the whole workspace for INVENTORY_ACCOUNTING_NOT_CLOSED (appears exactly once, in the blocker that reads this check, never in a test) and for any call to InventoryReport::is_closed() outside its own implementation (none).
gap_discovered_by: Self-directed audit, prompted by noticing core/src/census/mod.rs has no #[cfg(test)] module at all despite defining InventoryReport::is_closed() -- a function with the exact same shape and real-world stakes (gating a coding-admission blocker) as CensusReport::is_closed()/NormalizationReport::is_closed(), both of which DO have dedicated tests including negative cases that deliberately break the invariant post-construction.
key_finding: core/src/census/mod.rs defines InventoryReport::new/accounted_total/is_closed with zero tests anywhere in the file or workspace. is_closed() == (accounted_total() == artifacts_total), where accounted_total() sums the dispositions map's values. Confirmed via grep that: (1) INVENTORY_ACCOUNTING_NOT_CLOSED, the blocker string this check gates in runtime::systemize, appears exactly once in the entire workspace -- in the blocker itself, never in a test; (2) no test anywhere calls InventoryReport::is_closed() directly. Since dispositions/artifacts_total are both pub fields, a value with a corrupted/stale relationship between them (e.g. round-tripped through a cached JSON file, or produced by a future code path that doesn't go through InventoryReport::new) is a real, constructible value of this type, not a hypothetical -- and nothing in the test suite would have caught a regression that made is_closed() vacuously true.
verification_before_acting: Read InventoryReport's real, current implementation (new/accounted_total/is_closed) directly, confirming the exact invariant it checks and that its only real production callers (adapter::inventory_source, adapter::inventory_declared_source, via InventoryReport::new) always keep it self-consistent -- so this generation closes a verification gap, not a live defect.

Grepped the whole workspace for InventoryReport::is_closed and for the INVENTORY_ACCOUNTING_NOT_CLOSED blocker string, confirming zero test coverage exists for this specific check, in contrast to its siblings.

Read CensusReport::is_closed()/NormalizationReport::is_closed()'s existing test coverage (core/src/schema/mod.rs) to confirm the established, already-battle-tested pattern this generation mirrors: one positive (freshly-constructed) case, and at least one negative case that deliberately breaks the invariant after construction and confirms is_closed() catches it.

Falsified via the established inverted-direction technique (no live bug to revert-and-confirm against): temporarily replaced is_closed()'s real body with `true` (the exact regression class this test defends against), confirmed both new negative tests failed with the expected panic message, then restored the real implementation from a byte-for-byte backup and confirmed git diff --stat showed only the intended test addition.

design_decisions.question: Fix production code, or add tests?
design_decisions.decision: Tests only. is_closed()'s current logic is correct (confirmed by reading it and by the falsification below); the gap is that nothing verifies it. Added a #[cfg(test)] module to core/src/census/mod.rs (the file's first) with three tests: the positive case (a freshly-built report is always closed), and two distinct negative cases (dispositions map corrupted independently of artifacts_total; artifacts_total corrupted independently of dispositions) -- covering both operands of the equality is_closed() checks, not just one.
